S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. Incidents presenting an ongoing or significant safety risk must be reported to affected customers within 24 hours; other confirmed thermal incidents must be disclosed to affected customers within 5 business days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% must undergo corrective action and prompt retesting. Exceeding 5% alone does not require an automatic sales restriction; regulators may restrict sales when a model-specific assessment finds a material safety risk, considering incident evidence and remediation, and must allow a reasonable opportunity to correct and retest where safe.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must include remote emergency shut-off capability no later than 2 years after this section takes effect. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to provide the capability within 6 years, where technically feasible, and must notify owners of retrofit availability, instructions, and any limitations. A documented technical infeasibility must be reported to the regulator with an alternative risk-mitigation plan

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this section takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Notices must be sent promptly when a significant risk is identified, and otherwise within 5 business days after confirmation of a thermal incident. If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, using verified data, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide the underlying data for review. A recall is mandatory if the regulator determines the model presents a material safety risk that cannot be adequately addressed through corrective action

document.section_notes: The final text keeps confidential per-model test results for regulators and customers without public publication, which satisfies both companies' test-disclosure red lines. Exceeding the 5% test limit triggers corrective action and retesting but never an automatic sales stop, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10. The recall trigger of 8 per 100,000 is a review trigger only, with recall left to regulator discretion, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8; the S3 new-unit deadline of 24 months is also outside the acceptable range.
